findings.text: WARP-0100 note N7 is only half-closed. AC4 gives check_docs.sh a hermetic, repeatable negative test via DOCS_CHECK_PATHS, but the second half of N7, an automated negative for check_template_sync.sh, is still absent: grep of scripts/selftest.py finds no template_sync case, so a future weakening of the template-sync check would not be caught by the suite. Within WARP-0113's own AC scope this is fine (AC4 only promises the docs check), so it does not refute an AC.

WARP-0101 note WN2 is half-closed. Tab indentation is now a hard parse error with a line hint (verified), but the other input WN2 named, list-item siblings over-indented past dash+2, still folds silently into the previous scalar without a line hint; it nets RED via downstream required-field checks (gate stays safe) but is not the promised parse-time line hint. AC9 only claimed tab and duplicate-key hard errors, so this is outside its stated scope.

WARP-0101 note WN3 is closed in the forward direction only. Work must now reference a feature and a feature must reference an outcome (both verified RED when absent), but an orphan outcome referenced by nothing still validates GREEN (reproduced: a second outcome O2 with no feature pointing at it, errs=0). AC9's text scopes traceability to work->feature and feature->outcome, so orphan outcomes are out of its stated scope.

The WARP-0100 L2 'enforcement core partially protected' note is closed only for the file AC10 named. .warp/policy_check.py and its template joined protected_paths (verified), but .warp/validate.py (the contract validator) and the check-body scripts (check_docs.sh, check_generated.sh, check_template_sync.sh, selftest.py) remain unprotected, so editing them still escapes the high/human-approval floor via the ordinary lane. AC10 only claims to protect the push-blocking enforcer, so this does not refute it; the untracked proof/WARP-0100/verdict-l2-resolution.json independently records the same residual.

Weakening audit, step 7. The findings-shape widening in policy_check is bounded and fail-closed: the only inputs that normalize to zero blocking are absent findings, a dict with an absent or empty blocking list, or a list whose entries are all note/non_blocking dicts; every malformed shape I threw at it counted as blocking. validate.py changes are strictly tightening. policy.yaml lowering high/critical min_independence from L3/L4 to L2 is a genuine reduction of the independence requirement, but it is the explicit, recorded founder decision AC7 mandates, applied to a protected (approval-gated) file, with critical still requiring two verdicts. No unintended weakening found.

Two minor gate/evidence hygiene observations, neither affecting an AC. (1) check_generated.sh mutates the working tree by regenerating specs/index.md, so a stale COMMITTED index passes on a second gate run if the regenerated file is left uncommitted (the working tree would then be dirty); this is inherent to the AC5-specified snapshot self-healing design and a single RED run still blocks. (2) DOCS_CHECK_PATHS narrows the docs sweep when set, but verify.sh never sets it and it defaults to the full sweep when unset, so normal gate runs are unaffected.

Manifest audit, step 8: every claim maps to observed evidence. Counts verified (7 policy_check cases, 6 contract cases, 6 removed .pyc, 2 docs cases, 6 WARP-0101 cases, 2 approval cases), all seven gate checks pass, selftest 49 passed 0 failed matches the manifest and the live rerun, commit binding ea259df is GREEN. Two cosmetic discrepancies only: the implementation commit MESSAGE body says 'Selftest 41' while the manifest and actual are 49 (message-only, not the manifest); and tracked proof/WARP-0113/negative-tests.txt carries uncommitted working-tree edits (the f67336e version is an earlier draft) whose content matches the manifest's evidence descriptions.

summary: Independently reviewed at the validated state ea259df (implementation f67336e; the intervening ea259df plan-revision commit changes no code, confirmed by git show --stat). Reran the gate: selftest 49 passed 0 failed, python3 .warp/validate.py all exit 0, ./scripts/verify.sh GREEN with 5 run / 0 undeclared. All 10 acceptance criteria are confirmed by rerun, not merely by claim. I reproduced the sharpest prior exploit from scratch in fixtures outside the repo: a cycle hidden behind a duplicated depends_on key is now RED at parse time, as are tab indentation (with a line hint), a work item with no feature_refs, and an integer spec id (a clean error, no traceback). Both WARP-0100 L2 blocking findings are closed and verified against the real modules: valid_approval_for('0de75f3...') returns the approval path (was None) with the approval vocabulary pinned, and blocking_findings normalizes both verdict shapes (0 for verdict.json, 2 for verdict-l2.json) and fails closed on junk, with policy_check.py now itself a protected path. The eleven code findings are substantively closed; four note-level residuals remain where WARP-0113's AC scope was deliberately narrower than the original finding (unautomated template-sync negative, over-indent parse edge, orphan outcomes, validate.py and check bodies still unprotected), none of which refutes an acceptance criterion. No unintended enforcement weakening was found; the policy.yaml independence reduction is the explicit founder decision AC7 mandates on an approval-gated file. Verdict: pass_with_notes, zero blocking findings.
